tasks.title: Numbering rows
tasks.statement: Number the products by ascending price: title, price, rn (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY price)). Prices are distinct; order by rn.
tasks.hint: OVER (ORDER BY …) sets the order within the window.

tasks.title: Numbering within a group
tasks.statement: Number the products within each category by descending price: category, title, price, rn (PARTITION BY category). Order by category, rn.
tasks.hint: PARTITION BY splits the rows into independent groups.

tasks.title: Most expensive in each category
tasks.statement: Output the single most expensive product in each category: category, title, price (ROW_NUMBER = 1); order by category.
tasks.hint: Window functions can't go in WHERE — wrap the query.

tasks.title: Top 2 in a category
tasks.statement: Output the two most expensive products of each category: category, title, price; order by category, then price descending.

tasks.title: RANK and ties
tasks.statement: Output title, stock and the rank rk by descending stock using RANK(); for equal stock the ranks are equal and a gap follows them. Order by rk, title.

tasks.title: DENSE_RANK
tasks.statement: The same with DENSE_RANK(): after equal values the next rank follows with no gap. Output title, stock, rk; order by rk, title.

tasks.title: Three ways of numbering
tasks.statement: For products by descending stock, output title, stock, rn (ROW_NUMBER with a secondary key title), rk (RANK), dr (DENSE_RANK); order by rn.

tasks.title: Quartiles
tasks.statement: Split the products into 4 groups by price with NTILE(4): title, price, q; order by price (prices are distinct).
tasks.hint: NTILE(n) splits the ordered rows into n nearly equal parts.

tasks.title: Previous row
tasks.statement: For the orders of customer 5 (customer_id = 5), output id, created, total and the previous order's amount prev_total (LAG by created, id); order by created, id.

tasks.title: Change from the previous
tasks.statement: For customer 5, output id and the change of the order amount from the previous one diff = total - LAG(total) (NULL for the first); order by created, id.

tasks.title: LAG with a default value
tasks.statement: LAG(expression, offset, default). For customer 5, output id, total and prev_total, substituting 0 for NULL on the first order.

tasks.title: Next row
tasks.statement: For customer 5, output id, created and the date of the next order next_created (LEAD); order by created, id.

tasks.title: Days between orders
tasks.statement: For customer 5, output id and the number of days since the previous order gap_days (the difference of julianday values, an integer); NULL for the first; order by created, id.

tasks.title: Running total
tasks.statement: Output the orders by date: id, created, total and the running sum running (SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY created, id)); order by created, id.

tasks.title: Running total per customer
tasks.statement: A running sum within each customer: customer_id, id, total, running (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY created, id); order by customer_id, created, id.

tasks.title: Running counter
tasks.statement: Output the order id and the order's sequence number in the year (COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY created, id)) as n; order by n.

tasks.title: Group sum beside the row
tasks.statement: Output id, customer_id, total and the sum of all of that customer's orders client_sum (SUM OVER PARTITION BY customer_id); order by id.
tasks.hint: Without ORDER BY in the window, the sum is taken over the whole group.

tasks.title: Order's share within the customer
tasks.statement: Output id and the order's share of the customer's order sum share as a percentage (ROUND to an integer): total * 100.0 / SUM(total) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id); order by id.

tasks.title: Group average
tasks.statement: Output title, category, price and the category's average price cat_avg (ROUND to an integer, AVG OVER PARTITION BY category); order by id.

tasks.title: Deviation from the average
tasks.statement: Output title and the difference between the price and the category average diff = price - AVG(price) OVER (PARTITION BY category) (ROUND to an integer); order by id.

tasks.title: Moving average
tasks.statement: A moving average of the order amount over the last three orders (including the current one): id, total, ma3 (ROUND to an integer, ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW); order by created, id.

tasks.title: First value
tasks.statement: For each order, output id, customer_id and the date of the customer's first order first_order (FIRST_VALUE(created) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY created, id)); order by id.

tasks.title: Last value
tasks.statement: Output id and the date of the customer's last order last_order. Hint: LAST_VALUE needs the frame ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING, otherwise the window ends at the current row. Order by id.
tasks.hint: The default frame runs from the start to the current row.

tasks.title: Running maximum
tasks.statement: Output id, total and the maximum amount among the orders up to and including the current one (MAX OVER ORDER BY created, id) as max_so_far; order by created, id.

tasks.title: Percent rank
tasks.statement: Output title, price and the cumulative share of products cheaper than or equal to the current one cd = ROUND(CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY price), 2); order by price.

tasks.title: Named window
tasks.statement: A named window: SELECT … WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price). Output title, category and RANK() OVER w as rk; order by category, rk, title.

tasks.title: Remove duplicates
tasks.statement: In logins a user has several records. Keep one per user (the earliest by day): user_id, day (ROW_NUMBER = 1); order by user_id.

tasks.title: Streaks
tasks.statement: Find the streaks of consecutive login days of each user: user_id, first_day, last_day, length (day − ROW_NUMBER gives the same value within a streak); order by user_id, first_day.
tasks.hint: Within a streak the difference day − row number is constant.

tasks.title: HR: rank in a department
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name, dept_id, salary and the salary place within the department rk (RANK, descending); skip employees without a department. Order by dept_id, rk, name.

tasks.title: HR: department leaders
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name and dept_id of the highest-paid employee of each department (salaries are distinct for the leader within a department); order by dept_id.

tasks.title: HR: deviation from the department average
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name, salary and the difference from the department average diff (ROUND to an integer); skip employees without a department; order by dept_id, name.

tasks.title: HR: share of the payroll
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name, dept_id and the share of the salary in the department payroll share as a percentage (ROUND to an integer); order by dept_id, name.

tasks.title: HR: hiring order
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name, hired and the hiring number within the department n (ROW_NUMBER by hired); skip employees without a department; order by dept_id, n.

tasks.title: School: student's place
tasks.statement: School database. For the year 2024, output course_id, student_id, score and the place within the course rk (DENSE_RANK by descending score; ignore NULL); order by course_id, rk, student_id.

tasks.title: School: student's progress
tasks.statement: School database. For student 1, output year, course_id, score and the previous grade in the same course prev (LAG by year, PARTITION BY course_id); order by course_id, year.

tasks.title: Movies: rating within a genre
tasks.statement: Movies database. Output title, genre, rating and the place within the genre rk (RANK by descending rating; ignore movies without a rating); order by genre, rk, title.

tasks.title: Movies: a director's timeline
tasks.statement: Movies database. For the movies of director Nolan (director_id = 1), output title, year and the year of the previous movie prev_year (LAG by year); order by year.

tasks.title: Movies: cumulative budget
tasks.statement: Movies database. For movies with a known budget, output title, budget and the cumulative budget by year cum (SUM OVER ORDER BY year, id); order by year, id.
